text:
maria: Heads-up - saw an OOM in staging during the long-context load test (context ~120k tokens). KV page memory climbed steadily and then we hit allocation failure. Logs attached below.

kevin: Ugh. Can you paste the kv stats and the stack trace?

maria: Sure:
```
kv.metrics -> pages_total: 1024, pages_used: 1011, frag_pct: 31, avg_page_sz: 7.8MB, kv_live_bytes: 8.1GB, kv_reserved: 10.0GB
profile: alloc growth +2.3GB over 30s during decode backprop; kernel=kv_page_commit
oom: failed alloc 256MB (attempted new page)
```

aj: That frag_pct is worrying. Fragmentation + eager page allocation for long ctx looks like the combo. Did we try prefix reuse heuristics?

maria: We rely on reuse but for this workload there are a lot of unique prefixes and the reuse hit rate dropped to ~6% so pages accumulate. Also batching heuristics created 32-token microbatches that still triggered new page commits.

sophie: Can we short-term mitigate without a full rollout? Ideas: 1) force soft-evict for pages not touched in last N tokens (e.g., 4k) 2) when memory approaches threshold, stop creating new pages and fall back to prefix recompute 3) add a small ephemeralfallback store on host RAM that compresses older KV pages (~x2 compression)

kevin: +1 to soft-evict and early stop allocating. We should also return a recoverable error (507) so callers can retry with smaller context or with keep_cache=false. We don't want silent tail latencies or full pod restarts.

lucas: For longer-term, we need better kernel selection around page commits. If sequence length distribution is skewed to long tails, prefer kernels that allocate per-chunk instead of full-page commits. Also tune batching: group requests by expected kv footprint, not just tokens.

maria: Quick patch I can try in staging now: 1) add a mem_threshold flag (85% of kv_reserved) 2) if mem > threshold, mark new allocations as "soft" - allow reuse only, avoid physical page commit; 3) increment a metric kv.alloc.blocked_count and return 507 for requests that would need a new page and have low reuse score.

aj: Sounds good. Also emit a counter for kv.evicted_pages and kv.compressed_pages. Add an alert for sustained kv.alloc.blocked_count > 10/min.

infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: docker image redwood/kv-runtime:canary-20260317 ready for staging deploy :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started to staging - rollout 10% nodes.

kevin: After the canary: please collect an allocation flamegraph and a kv page histogram. If we see fragmentation > 25% after 10 minutes, abort and rollback.

maria: Running canary now. Quick note on heuristics: I implemented a reuse_score = recent_hits / (1 + unique_prefix_count) and the alloc code will prefer reuse_score>0.15 for committing. If below, it'll try to evict LRU candidates or mark as compressed.

sophie: Nice. Also let's make the client SDK tolerant: SDK can detect 507 + header Retry-After and automatically retry with keep_cache=false and batch_size=1 for the failed request path. We should coordinate with devex.

lucas: Postmortem items to track: - root cause: low reuse on longCtx workload + eager commit path - mitigations: soft-alloc circuit, compressed host pages, SDK retry path - followups: kernel selection by footprint, smarter batching sharding by kv estimate, runtime-level compact-on-idle.

maria: Canary ran 10m: blocked_count spiked briefly then returned to 0. No OOMs. kv.evicted_pages = 142, kv.compressed_pages = 38. Fragmentation dropped from 31% -> 24% during canary.

kevin: Great. Schedule a limited rollout to prod next (30% nodes), keep alert thresholds tight. Add an integration test that simulates unique-prefix-heavy workload to avoid regressions.

aj: I'll own the prod rollout + dashboards. I'll add a graph for kv.alloc.blocked_count and kv.alloc.failed_retries.

maria: Filed follow-ups in the runtime board: compact-on-idle RFC, kernel selection experiment, SDK retry patch. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
